items.title: Eric Alexander interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 31, 2010
items.q: Johnny Griffin and George Coleman, all these cats, Dexter Gordon.

ctx.x: Nice. And I agree with what you’re saying. Like you did the tune “It’s Magic,” and it’s exactly what you’re saying when I saw that I go he did “It’s Magic”? Like and then I start to sing the song in my head and I go wow, what an interesting choice. I can’t wait to hear what you did with that.

Yeah. And I would be the same way too, I mean I often say, okay, let’s say I’m at a jazz festival and these guys all come back from the beyond for the greatest jam session ever. You know, it’s Coltrane, Sonn — well Sonny Rollins he’s here, so Sonny’s there and whatever, Johnny Griffin and George Coleman, all these cats, Dexter Gordon. And then the program starts and it’s five originals that I’ve never heard before and I can’t even figure out what the chord changes are. Would I enjoy that? No. What do I want to…

major 7 flat 5, and then it goes down a minor third and it’s an inverted strange triad with a strange extension. And by the time I get to the end of the tune I’ve figured out a few chords and the time signature and I haven’t heard one thing that the people have played because I’ve spent the whole time trying to get my bearings so that I could understand it a little bit. And I don’t know how the casual listeners are reacting favorably to it because I can’t believe that they could be enjoying it as much as they…
